description: Shape of one entry in the optimization-pattern library. filter_patterns.py selects eligible patterns by matching these fields against the optimizer_input.json unit (class/pattern), its allowed_transformation_families, and the optimization_policy flags. The LLM then picks one eligible pattern by id. Versioned so logged runs stay attributable when a template changes.

id.description: Stable unique id, e.g. 'arith.balanced_adder_tree'. The LLM returns this in chosen_pattern_id.

family.description: Must be one of the unit's allowed_transformation_families for the pattern to be eligible.

applies_when.description: Preconditions matched against the optimizer_input unit/region.

class.description: Structural classes this fits, e.g. ['arithmetic']. Empty = any.

pattern_in.description: classify_path patterns this fits, e.g. ['adder','adder_followed_by_mux']. Empty = any.

requires_flags.description: optimization_policy flags that must all be true.

latency_effect.description: 'preserves' patterns are offered under the default policy; 'changes' patterns are filtered OUT unless allow_latency_change is true. This is an offer-time policy filter, not an equivalence guarantee. Equivalence is established only by verify_rtl.py after a candidate exists.

sec_recipe.description: The verification mode/recipe that must be run for this pattern's class of change; it is a requirement, not a proof result.

template.description: Short natural-language description of the before->after transform.

example.description: One worked before/after pair, used as a few-shot exemplar in the request.

guardrails.description: Hard DON'Ts injected into the prompt.

expected_equivalence_class.description: Selects the verification mode expected for this class of change. It is a policy expectation and makes no claim about the eventual proof outcome.
